correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed all quantifiers and domain restrictions. Finite ring radical is nilpotent and nilpotency lifts through it, giving equality of conditional right-partner propensities under reduction. For fixed rank-r matrix, the induced random restriction to its image is uniform End(F_q^r), yielding probability q^{-r} using a complete Fitting-decomposition count q^{r²-r}. Gaussian rank counts establish the full law, a kernel expectation gives the exact mean, and a strict chord inequality plus independent-factor replacement proves the sharp convex-order/equality criterion. Exact arithmetic checks of full multiplication tables agree, without being used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The nilpotent-product probability newly studied in 2026 is a scalar that fails to separate a noncommutative matrix ring from an equal-order commutative local ring. The complete conditional partner-propensity law for every finite unital ring and its sharp convex-order comparison supply a natural nontrivial structural refinement. Strict variance contraction exactly detects a noncommutative simple block in the semisimple quotient; in the 2-by-2 family the variance ratio is exactly 1/(q+1). This is a complete infinite-family classification with motivated mathematical use, not a renamed scalar formula.
